message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the most common way to spin up a VM) and also shows the equivalent **REST API** call (in case you want to embed it in a script or a Terraform provider).

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** are enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have a suitable **zone** that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> * You have a **service account** or the default account with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or higher).  

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to suit your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pull the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--boot-disk-type=pd-ssd` | Use SSD for better I/O. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: run a startup script (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers). |
| `--scopes` | Grant the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers). |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic if you plan to expose services. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just increase `GPU_COUNT`.  
> **Tip:** For a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-8`), replace the `--machine-type` value.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly, here’s a minimal example.  
First, obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token:

```bash
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
```

Then send the POST request:

```bash
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances?alt=json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Note:**  
> * The `acceleratorType` field uses the fully‑qualified resource name.  
> * The `metadata` section can include a `startup-script` that installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.  
> * Adjust `machineType`, `diskSizeGb`, and other fields as needed.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE"

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see an entry for **NVIDIA RTX A6000** with the correct driver version.

---

## 4. Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “GPU quota exceeded” | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| “Accelerator type not found” | Ensure the zone supports the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator. |
| “Driver not installed” | Use the startup script to install the NVIDIA driver, or manually run `sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535`. |
| “Instance fails to start” | Check the serial console logs via the Cloud Console → Compute Engine → VM instances → Serial port 1 (console). |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

That’s all you need to spin up a GPU‑enabled Ubuntu 20.04 VM on Google Cloud!
